seo.title: CrossBeamIP — Run your IP portfolio without the spreadsheet
seo.description: CrossBeamIP keeps docketing, annuities and prior-art research in one system, so in-house IP teams stop reconciling four spreadsheets before every filing deadline.

sections.heading: Every deadline, every family, one system of record
sections.body: CrossBeamIP replaces the docketing spreadsheet, the annuity reminder inbox and the shared drive of prior-art PDFs with a single portfolio your whole team reads from.

sections.heading: What in-house IP teams actually run on
sections.intro: Four capabilities that cover the work between an invention disclosure and a granted, maintained right.

items.title: Docketing that reconciles itself
items.body: Office actions, responses and statutory bars are dated from the source register, not retyped from an email. Conflicts surface as a diff you approve.

items.title: Annuity forecasting in currency
items.body: Three-year renewal cost projections per jurisdiction, with the abandon/maintain decision recorded against the family so finance stops asking twice.

items.title: Prior-art workspace
items.body: Search results, examiner citations and your own notes live on the family record, so the next attorney to touch it inherits the reasoning.

items.title: Outside-counsel handoff
items.body: Instruction letters generated from the docket entry, with a read receipt and a due date the firm sees in the same view you do.

sections.heading: Bring your portfolio over in a fortnight
sections.body: Send us a docket export in any format your current provider gives you. We map it, you review the diff, and nothing goes live until the dates reconcile.
sections.footnote: No card, no trial clock — migration review is done with a real engineer.

seo.title: Product overview — docketing, annuities and prior art in one record | CrossBeamIP
seo.description: See how CrossBeamIP models an IP family: register-sourced dates, renewal forecasts, prior-art notes and outside-counsel instructions on a single record.

sections.heading: One family record, four teams reading it
sections.body: Paralegals docket against it, attorneys reason on it, finance forecasts from it and outside counsel is instructed from it. There is no second copy to reconcile.

sections.heading: How the record is put together
sections.intro: Each capability writes to the same family object, which is why the numbers agree across screens.

items.title: Register-sourced dating
items.body: Priority, filing, publication and grant dates are pulled from the national register and versioned. When a register corrects itself, you see the correction as an event, not a silent overwrite.

items.title: Rule engine per jurisdiction
items.body: Response windows, extension options and annuity schedules encoded per office. A rule change ships as a dated update you can see in the family's history.

items.title: Cost model attached to the family
items.body: Official fees, agent fees and translation costs sit on the record in the filing currency and the reporting currency, both at the rate on the date incurred.

items.title: Instruction letters with receipts
items.body: Generate the letter from the docket entry, send it, and keep the acknowledgement on the same record. No hunting through a shared mailbox for who confirmed what.

items.title: Audit trail that survives people leaving
items.body: Every status change carries who, when and the reasoning field they filled in. Handover stops depending on one paralegal's memory.

items.title: Exports that go back out cleanly
items.body: WIPO ST.96, CSV and your finance system's chart of accounts. Migrating away later is a supported operation, not a support ticket.

sections.heading: See it against your own docket
sections.body: We run a read-only import of a slice of your portfolio and show you where our dates disagree with your current ones. That report is yours either way.
sections.footnote: Typical slice is 200 families and takes four working days.

seo.title: Pricing — per family, per year, no seat tax | CrossBeamIP
seo.description: CrossBeamIP is priced per IP family under management, not per seat, so adding a paralegal or an outside firm to a matter costs nothing extra.

sections.heading: Priced per family, not per seat
sections.body: Everyone who touches a matter — paralegals, attorneys, finance, outside counsel — gets a login at no extra cost. You pay for the portfolio you actually manage.

sections.heading: Three tiers, one product
sections.intro: The same record model at every tier. What changes is the jurisdiction coverage and how much of the migration we do for you.

items.title: Docket — $12 per family / year
items.body: Register-sourced dating and deadline management for up to 8 jurisdictions. Self-serve CSV import. Email support with a one-business-day target.

items.title: Portfolio — $18 per family / year
items.body: All 42 jurisdictions, annuity forecasting, cost model and outside-counsel instructions. Assisted migration with a reconciliation report before cutover.

items.title: Enterprise — from $26 per family / year
items.body: Adds SSO, custom retention policy, sandbox tenant and a named migration engineer. Annual invoicing and a signed DPA as standard.

items.title: What is never metered
items.body: Users, matters viewed, documents stored, API calls and exports. We have never found a way to price those that did not punish good practice.

sections.heading: Work out your number in about a minute
sections.body: Count the live families in your current docket, multiply by the tier rate. If the answer surprises you, tell us the count and we will sanity-check it against portfolios the same shape.
sections.footnote: Dormant and abandoned families are not billed.

seo.title: Portfolio analytics — decide what to renew and what to let lapse | CrossBeamIP
seo.description: Model renewal cost against commercial coverage per family, so the abandon-or-maintain decision is made on evidence and recorded where the next reviewer will find it.

sections.heading: Know which quarter of the portfolio is paying for itself
sections.body: Most portfolios carry 20–30% of families that no product line depends on any more. Analytics finds them before the annuity invoice does.

sections.heading: What the analytics actually answer
sections.intro: Four questions IP counsel gets asked by a CFO, with the working shown.

items.title: What will renewals cost us for the next three years?
items.body: Forecast by jurisdiction and by business unit, in the currency each entity reports in, with the fee schedule version stamped on the number.

items.title: Which families protect a product we still sell?
items.body: Link families to product lines once; the coverage map stays current as the docket moves. Unlinked families are flagged, not hidden.

items.title: Where are we filing more than we need to?
items.body: Jurisdiction overlap by family, so a routine five-country filing strategy gets tested against where revenue actually is.

items.title: What did we decide last time, and why?
items.body: Every abandon/maintain decision keeps its reasoning and its author. The review a year later starts from that, not from scratch.

sections.heading: Start with one renewal cycle
sections.body: Give us the families with annuities due in the next two quarters. We return the coverage map and the forecast, and you keep it whether or not you continue.
sections.footnote: Runs read-only against an export — no access to your live system required.

title: Blog — Why we moved 44 pages off edit.site

seo.title: Why we moved 44 marketing pages off edit.site | CrossBeamIP Blog
seo.description: A visual site builder got our marketing site launched. It also made every copy change a 44-page find-and-replace. Here is what we moved to and what it cost.

sections.heading: Why we moved 44 marketing pages off edit.site
sections.body: The builder was not the problem. Forty-four independent copies of the same header was the problem, and no builder was going to fix that for us.

sections.heading: What we learned doing it
sections.intro: Four things we would tell anyone about to hand-copy a marketing site into a framework.

items.title: Hand-copying 44 pages produces 44 pages of debt
items.body: The second page you copy is where the divergence starts. We modelled content first and got three section types that covered every page we had.

items.title: The redirect map is the migration
items.body: Every old URL had inbound links and ranking. We wrote the legacy-to-new map before writing a single page, and every one of them answers 308 today.

items.title: Metadata belongs to the content, not the template
items.body: Title, description, canonical and OG come off the page record through generateMetadata. Nobody can ship a page with the previous page's title again.

items.title: An inventory you can filter beats a migration plan nobody opens
items.body: Status and priority per page, shareable via the URL, visible to whoever asks. That console is what let us stop holding the plan in a spreadsheet.

sections.heading: The console in this post is live
sections.body: The migration console lists all 44 pages, tracks status per row, and links straight through to the five pages that are fully migrated so far.
sections.footnote: Statuses you set are yours — they ride in a cookie on your own browser.
